The test image shows a very young soybean seedling (just emerged) collapsed flat on dark, moist soil with yellowish-brown, wilted cotyledons — classic post-emergence damping-off. Comparing to references:

- **Pythium_damping_off**: Direct match — same seedling stage, same collapsed-on-moist-soil presentation, same yellowed/soft cotyledons
- **Rhizoctonia**: Shows reddish-brown, firm/dry sunken lesions on hypocotyl — not present here
- **Phytophthora**: Affects older plants, dark brown stem lesion extending up from taproot
- **Fusarium**: Root/vascular browning in older plants
- **Phomopsis/Anthracnose/Diaporthe**: Pod/stem diseases of mature plants

The moist soil, very early seedling stage, and soft collapsed cotyledons all point to Pythium damping-off.
